test_title: SSC CPO 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 04 Oct, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In which year Timur’s invasion of Delhi took place?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1398**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Timur,** also known as Tamerlane, led an **invasion of northern India** in **1398**, targeting the **Delhi Sultanate** ruled by Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq of the **Tughlaq dynasty**.
 
• Crossing the Indus River on **September 30, 1398,** Timur sacked Tulamba and carried out a **brutal massacre of its inhabitants**.
 
• Born on April 9, 1336, Timur was a Turco-Mongol conqueror who founded the Timurid Empire across modern-day Afghanistan, Iran, and Central Asia.
 
• He claimed descent from **Genghis Khan** and embraced Islam during his reign as the** first ruler of the Timurid dynasty**.
 
• Timur's military campaigns left a significant impact on the history of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In 1398, amidst internal feuds among **Feroz Shah's successors** threatening the empire's stability, Timur invaded India from the north, effectively dismantling the centralized rule of Delhi.
 
• His conquest included the destruction of the **Turkish Sultanate of Delhi,** marked by the execution of at least 50,000 captives before the Battle of Delhi.
 
• Additionally, around 100,000 residents of Delhi were taken as slaves after the battle. Timur's campaign resulted in the estimated slaughter of up to 100,000 natives, and his forces marched as far as the Ganges before his return due to issues in Western Asia.
 
• Following the invasion and plundering of Delhi, Timur retired to Samarqand, leaving behind a significant Uzbek genetic influence in North India.
 
• Throughout his conquests, which spanned Persia, Khorasan, Jurjan, Afghanistan, and Azerbaijan, Timur earned the epithet "Prince of Destruction" for his devastating military campaigns.
